content: Is it intentional that there is not a docgen release for v4.29.0-rc1 corresponding to the PR moving to this toolchain?
This was an accident, fixed by one more execution of script/release_checklist.py v4.29.0-rc1 in the lean4 repo.
Was there a similar issue for v4.29.0-rc6? This release seems to be missing as well.
doc-gen4 has not yet reached v4.29.0-rc6, see https://github.com/leanprover/doc-gen4/pull/369.

My question is because the documentation for CSLib is currently failing because docgen-action is looking for this release. Is this a problem with the logic in docgen-action for determining the release to use, or do we need to do something on our end to prevent this?

(But yes, if doc-gen reaches a toolchain later than Mathlib or CSLib does, we expect docgen builds to fail in the meantime. The alternative would be to gate moving these libraries to the toolchain until doc-gen reaches it. I don't want to do this for Mathlib, and don't mind either way for CSLib.)
Thanks! I'll consider if we want to add a check for this.

When I looked at the Mathlib docs during this time the landing page indicated the usual "built using Lean 4 4.29.0-rc6", which I found a bit confusing. Was it able to use the previous toolchain docgen in this interim? (I wasn't sure where to find those logs to check myself.)
Sorry, I couldn't be sure without digging through logs.
